description: MIXING and MASTERING: mix the stems instead of summing them: each part levelled for how loud it plays, panned, high-passed, given its depth on a shared reverb, and mastered to a loudness target — returned as a WAV AND as `mixgraph`, the mix as a document you edit. After doseedo_render_score pass from_job (its parts and the instruments they play are the stems); or stems: [{name, audio_url, instrument?}] (result links work as-is). An orchestra (strings / winds / brass / timpani / harp…) is SEATED by default (film-orchestral: violins left, low strings right, winds centre, brass behind, each seat with its own depth in a 2.3 s hall, written dynamics riding the faders; room / dynamics_ride change that); other stems get the blind default. style: film-orchestral, film-scoring-stage, concert-hall, film-epic-hybrid, cathedral-choral, classical-chamber, jazz-combo, ambient, country-pop, metal-modern, 1950s-mono, 1960s-lcr-pop, 1970s-analog-rock, 1970s-dub, 1980s-pop-gated, 1990s-rock-dry, 1990s-hiphop, 2000s-loudness-rock, 2010s-edm, 2010s-trap, 2020s-pop, 2020s-hyperpop — an id or words ("dry 90s rock"). balance {part: dB} moves parts on top of the levelling (+3 brings a melody forward). Change the mix: edit the returned mixgraph — strips[] {stem, gain_db, pan, seat, chain, sends}, buses[] (verb = the hall), master.chain, automation [{target: "strips.<stem>.gain_db", points: [[seconds, dB]…]}] for rides — and call again with mixgraph + the same from_job / stems: rendered as written (safety rails still apply and are reported), no credits. report.strips.<part>.active_lufs = how loud each part plays in the mix. Then doseedo_session_from_stems {from_job, mix_job: <this job_id>} → the DAW project at this mix's levels and pans. Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (~15–90 s). Cancel: the plane has no stop for a running mix — it runs to completion (credits spent), the job ends as canceled and its output is discarded. Only a job still queued at the plane is refunded by the plane's own failure refund.

balance.description: {part name: dB in -12..12} — your balance on top of the levelling (and of the written dynamics a from_job reads).

dynamics.description: Fader rides from written dynamics: {part name: [[onset_seconds, velocity 0-127], …]}. from_job fills it from the score (pp to ff ≈ 17 dB); pass {} for no rides.

dynamics_ride.description: How hard the written dynamics move the faders: 1 = default (pp to ff ≈ 17 dB), 0 = no rides, up to 1.5.

from_job.description: MCP: a doseedo_render_score job_id — its parts are the stems, each with the instrument it plays, and each part's written dynamics (its mean velocity) set its balance.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

mixgraph.description: An edited mix — the mixgraph a doseedo_mix returned, changed — rendered against the same stems (from_job or stems). Omit for a fresh mix.

room.description: An orchestra's room: "studio" (intimate scoring stage, ~1.2 s, close), "stage" (~1.8 s), "hall" (the default scoring hall, ~2.3 s), "cathedral" (~4 s, wet) — or 0..1 between them. Sets the decay, size and how wet every seat sits.

stems.description: [{name, audio_url, instrument?}] — the stems (≤ 32). instrument = the sound it plays (a doseedo_instruments id: "violin", "timpani", "harp"), which decides how it is mixed; without it the name decides.

style.description: A mix style: an id (film-orchestral, classical-chamber, jazz-combo, ambient, 1970s-analog-rock, 2020s-pop …) or words ("dry 90s rock"). Default: film-orchestral for an orchestra, else the blind default.

target_lufs.description: Master loudness, -24..-6 LUFS (default: the style's — -18 for film-orchestral, -14 for the blind default).

tonal_match.description: Nudge the master toward professionally mixed orchestral references (default on for the orchestral styles).

name: doseedo_mix
title: Mix and master stems
